input.message:
Review of 2be494c (branch work-branch), scope per brief. Recalled memorygraph first (hits c8fb1db0 /rest/user cap, be9bfb6c fixed-ip design, 0ddd2f41 PUT hypothesis). I did not run unifi-api.sh live and changed nothing in the worktree (mutants ran in a scratchpad copy of scripts/, stubbed curl/op, UNIFI_HOST and LAB_SSH_HOST unset-then-stubbed by the selftest's own env).

Lint: `./scripts/lint.sh --changed HEAD~1` rc=0. shellcheck clean 130/130, PASS=14 FAIL=0, selftest lane 18 of 18 (unifi-api-selftest.sh is in it). known-issue lint SKIPPED (no ai-toolkit checkout beside the repo), so that gate is unevaluated, not passed.

Gate note (API-facing script): the diff and PROVENANCE.md evidence only read-only raw GETs for the fixtures. No recorded live `fixed-ip --dry-run` run and no recorded live write loop appear in HEAD. If the ticket carries a pasted live `--dry-run` run, the author must cite it. See finding 1.

Findings (path:line, severity, problem, fix owner is author):

1. scripts/api/unifi-api.sh:cmd_fixed_ip PUT path (about line 285-297) -- HIGH -- the write path is UNPROVEN against the real controller. PUT /rest/user/<_id> with {use_fixedip,network_id,fixed_ip} and the `.meta.rc == "ok"` success test were never exercised live; the PUT response fixture is `put.ok.json` = `{"meta":{"rc":"ok"},"data":[]}` typed by hand in the selftest (line 140). Item 13: authored stub shape. Memory 0ddd2f41 itself labels PUT /rest/user/<_id> "hypothesis". CLAUDE.md spike rule asks for a live write loop on a scratch client first. Failing case to show: one real PUT against a scratch client with its response recorded as fixtures/unifi-api/put-rest-user.200.json, and a real PUT rejection recorded for the `.meta.msg` path. Until then "verified read-back" is a claim, not an observation.

2. scripts/api/unifi-api-selftest.sh (mutation survivors) -- MEDIUM -- three mutants of unifi-api.sh pass the whole selftest with 0 FAILs: (a) drop `and .network_id == $n` from the already-held ("unchanged") predicate; (b) drop `and .network_id == $n` from the read-back verification; (c) change `length == 1` to `length >= 1` in fetch_client. Meaning: a client holding the right IP on the wrong network is reported "unchanged" and never written, and a read-back where network_id did not stick is reported "verified". No fixture has fixed_ip right with network_id wrong, and none has a 2-record /stat/user response. The header comment's mutation list never covered these fields, and network_id is one of the "three fields" the header promises are verified. Need cases that fail on each of these.

3. scripts/api/unifi-api-selftest.sh:194 -- LOW -- `check "read-back reads /stat/user" "$LAST_LOG" "GET .../stat/user/$MAC"` is non-discriminating: the initial lookup already logs that exact line, so it passes even with no read-back. Header line 16 lists it as the oracle that kills "read back from /rest/user/<id>"; in fact that mutant is caught only incidentally by the exit-0 and "read-back differs" assertions. Claim is mislabelled; assert on a count of 2 GETs.

4. scripts/api/unifi-api.sh:cap block (about line 258-261) -- MEDIUM -- completeness of the other-holder set is not proven, only one number is refused. The check is `n == 0 || n == 3000`. Mutant `n -ge 2999` also passes the selftest, and any silent truncation at another size (a different cap, a paged or time-windowed response) passes the check. Item 12: no independent oracle. One available independent probe is that the target MAC (already read whole from /stat/user/<mac>) must appear in the /stat/alluser set; its absence means the set is incomplete. Note also the measured 3000 cap was on /rest/user; /stat/alluser measured 9011, so the "cap" test models a limit nobody has seen on this endpoint. State that in the header, or the "visible failure if the set cannot be read whole" requirement is met only for the one number.

5. scripts/fixtures/unifi-api/PROVENANCE.md + selftest:139 -- MEDIUM -- the HTTP 400 api.err.UnknownUser body is synthetic (`{"meta":{"rc":"error","msg":"api.err.UnknownUser"},"data":[]}`). The shape is disclosed, and the wrapper's own recorded line shows the token arrives in the message, so risk is bounded, but item 13 wants a recorded body. The script's two branches depend on REQ_CODE=400 plus a grep of the file; a body whose token sits somewhere other than raw text would still match, one where the wrapper's `.meta.msg` was derived differently would not be seen. Record it with `unifi-api.sh raw /stat/user/02:00:00:00:00:01` (read-only, owner/orchestrator run) or accept explicitly in the ticket.

6. scripts/fixtures/unifi-api/stat-alluser.trimmed.200.json -- LOW -- the recorded alluser fixture has `network_id: null` on all three records, and 3 of 9011 records were kept. The cap fixture is one record repeated 3000 times (same MAC), so the "complete set" path is never exercised with distinct holders and the target record at an arbitrary position. Fine for the cap, thin for holder search.

7. scripts/api/unifi-api.sh (file header / design) -- MEDIUM (pre-existing, not introduced by this commit) -- read-only API client carries a write subcommand, item 7. The write belongs in a sibling script. This commit deepens it (--force, read-back). Decide explicitly or file the split.

8. scripts/api/unifi-api.sh dry-run block -- LOW -- `--dry-run` still logs in and issues three GETs (networkconf, stat/user, stat/alluser). Not a bug; the isolation guard is the *_HOST variables, which the selftest does set. Mentioned only because dry-run output prints a `jq -c '{_id,mac,name,hostname,use_fixedip,fixed_ip,network_id}'` projection (allow-listed, no secrets), which is correct.

Clean checks (observed, not read): other-holder refused, also under --force, no PUT (selftest 217-222, and mutant dropping use_fixedip from the holder filter fails the "stale fixed_ip" case); exact-3000 and empty set refused with no PUT (mutants fail 3 and 2 assertions); dry-run sends no PUT; unknown MAC dies with named message; non-canonical IPs rejected by ip_to_int; MAC lowercased; CSRF token not in argv (stub logs argv). Bash 3.2: no violations seen. Vault: login uses op_field with item, labkit default vault.

Verdict: SHIP WITH FIXES. Blocking: 1 (live write loop and recorded PUT response; until then the first real PUT is the owner's, which is the process defect the CLAUDE.md rule names) and 2 (network_id never asserted anywhere in the held/read-back paths). 4 should be answered in the ticket (either add the target-present oracle or document why equality-to-3000 suffices). 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 non-blocking.

Paths: <worktree>/scripts/api/unifi-api.sh, <worktree>/scripts/api/unifi-api-selftest.sh, <worktree>/scripts/fixtures/unifi-api/PROVENANCE.md.
